history.title: Agent Incident Ledger: Filed Reports vs Blank Pages

style_when: the story is regulatory or contractual — a filing, a mandate, a rate notice, a certificate, a purchase order that changed the economics
prompt: Top-down flat-lay photograph on a brushed-steel control room desk, split-screen diptych with hard left-right contrast. Left half: a dense, neatly squared stack of filed issue reports, stamped covers, paperclipped corners, tactile bone-white paper stock, brightly lit. Right half: an open incident ledger logbook, its recent ruled pages blank, falling into shadow, one small oxidised-red flag marker lying unused on the empty page. A single soft directional light enters from the left edge of the frame and dies before the ledger. Graphite, bone white, oxidised red. 50mm, top-down 90-degree view, gentle vignette falloff, muted paper tones, blank and illegibly cropped pages, fine film grain, no people, no logos.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, readable print, watermarks, logos
rationale: The story's entire evidence chain is documentary — the Agent Incident Ledger, 861 issue reports, status pages, disclosures — so the artefact is the protagonist, and a top-down still life of the record itself is the truest embodiment. The split-screen diptych with light falling only on the filed half literally shows the detectors aimed at the wrong half: dense paper under the lamp, blank ledger pages in the dark.
cue: aimed at the wrong half of the failure surface
subject: an incident ledger's blank recent pages beside a stack of filed issue reports
core_thesis: Static agent-failure detection just hit 91% precision on the bugs that file issues, while the median real agent incident waits 66 days for disclosure — the detectors are sharpening the wrong half of the failure surface.
core_conflict: 91% precision on failures that leave a bug report vs the 66-day silence of failures that leave nothing to read
composition: split-screen diptych with left-right contrast: dense filed reports lit on the left, blank open ledger in shadow on the right
alt_text: 91% Precision, 66 Days Late. Filed issue reports in bright light beside an open incident ledger with blank pages and an unused red flag
caption: 91% Precision, 66 Days Late: Detection races ahead on agent failures that leave logs, not the ones that carry risk.
title: 91% Precision, 66 Days Late

review.depicts: A stack of white paper sheets held together by metal binder clips under a bright light on the left, beside an open blank notebook with a small red bookmark tab in shadow on the right.
review.reason: The image delivers the ordered frame's own objects — a lit stack of filed paper reports contrasted with a shadowed blank open ledger — which maps directly onto the article's point that issues get filed while incidents go unrecorded, though the reports themselves are blank rather than dense with text.
